title: Learning Pathways
text: Identify which learning pathway you want to pursue and explain the steps required to succeed in it.
cdi_links: 4.E.03 Recognising the main learning pathways and considering which one they want to follow and how they will access and succeed in it

title: Introduction
text: In this lesson, you will explore
bullets: Different learning pathways available after school
How to decide which pathway suits your goals
Entry requirements for different pathways
How to plan steps to succeed in your chosen route

title: Success Criteria
bullets: I can identify a learning pathway that interests me
I can explain the entry requirements for that pathway
I can describe possible careers linked to the pathway
I can plan steps that will help me succeed

title: Key Words
bullets: Entry Requirements – The qualifications or skills needed to start a course or job.
Action Plan – A step-by-step guide you create to help you reach a goal.
Success Strategy – A personal approach to achieving goals in education or work.
Aspirations – Your hopes or ambitions for the future.

title: Supported Internships
bullets: Supported Internships are designed for learners aged 16–24 with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).
Students gain real workplace experience with support from job coaches and tutors.
Common sectors include retail, hospitality, administration, facilities, and animal care.
This pathway suits students who learn best through hands-on experience and structured support.

title: College Pathway
bullets: College provides practical learning and vocational qualifications.
Courses may include BTECs, T Levels, and Level 2–3 certificates.
Common sectors include trades, hair and beauty, hospitality, sport, and health and social care.
College suits learners who want hands-on training or a pathway to further study.

title: Apprenticeship Pathway
bullets: Apprenticeships allow you to work while training and earning a wage.
They combine real work experience with recognised qualifications.
Common sectors include construction, motor vehicle, business administration, digital, and retail.
This pathway suits learners who prefer learning by doing.

title: University Pathway
bullets: University is often chosen for careers that require higher level qualifications.
Common sectors include healthcare, engineering, science, education, and creative industries.
A degree is usually the minimum entry requirement for these professions.
University suits learners who want academic study leading to specialist careers.

title: Activity – Explore a Pathway
text: Choose one of the main learning pathways after school.

title: Reflection
bullets: Which pathway feels like the best match for your interests?
What steps will you need to take to access this pathway?
What skills or qualifications should you start developing now?

title: Complete the sentence
sentence: Researching reliable information helps you make better ________ about education and career routes.

title: Key Takeaways
bullets: Different learning pathways lead to different careers
Understanding entry requirements helps you prepare early
Planning your next steps helps you move towards your goals
